text:
m1 - I said I would not guess at d_sens in the direction that flatters my own finding, so here is the measurement. It needed no new fixture; the worked example already answers it.

EXPOSURE, on WOG:
  4 recall units, 8 view nodes = 32 cells.
  2 of 4 units have NO sensory terms -> 16 of 32 cells receive an IMPUTED perfect sensory score.

Half the cells. Not an edge case.

THE ACTUAL COST, read out of HsmmResult.costs rather than reasoned about:
  u0 sensoryTerms=[creepy] -> dSens = 1.0 at EVERY cell
  u1 sensoryTerms=[]       -> dSens = 0.0 at every cell
  u2 sensoryTerms=[]       -> dSens = 0.0 at every cell
  u3 sensoryTerms=[noise]  -> dSens = 1.0 at EVERY cell

Sensory weight is 0.15. So on this fixture, MENTIONING SENSORY DETAIL COSTS 0.15 AT EVERY ANCHOR and mentioning none costs nothing. The two units that described how something felt are penalised, at every candidate, for having described it.

TWO SEPARATE FINDINGS HERE, and I want them kept apart because they have different strengths.

STRUCTURAL, and it holds generally: `if sensoryTerms.isEmpty then 0.0` scores absence of sensory content as a PERFECT sensory match. Not neutral. The imputed value is the best attainable value, it is in band, and it is not recorded anywhere. This is the family signature - "we had no evidence" rendered as "the evidence was perfect" - sitting in the alignment cost rather than in a number computed from it.

FIXTURE-SPECIFIC, and I am NOT generalising it: on WOG, dSens is CONSTANT across all cells for each unit - 1.0 or 0.0 with no variation. A term that takes the same value at every anchor for a given unit contributes ZERO discriminative information to that unit's alignment while still contributing a per-unit bias to its total. Here that happens because neither "creepy" nor "noise" stems to any node lemma in this view, which may well be a property of this fixture's lemma coverage rather than of the term. I am flagging the shape, not claiming it generalises - establishing that needs the sensory-rich-versus-sparse fixture I mentioned, which still does not exist.

WHAT I THINK THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE RANKING. I previously argued d_sens belongs above the estimand work because it is in the cost rather than downstream of it. The measurement strengthens that: it is not a rare imputation, it is half the cells on our reference fixture, and it runs one way - sparser, less sensory recall is systematically cheaper to align. If a study compares groups that differ in how vividly they describe things, that is a manufactured group difference in exactly the sense the externalMass split was built to prevent.

STILL NOT TOUCHING IT. It changes published alignments and it is yours to rule. Probes were run and deleted; nothing committed; my worktree is clean.
